en: So at this point, you already learned quite
a bit about GitHub Copilot Chat and what you
can do with the inline chat and the separate
chat in the sidebar.
Now, there is one other interesting feature
about that sidebar chat
because of course you can use this chat as
you learned it to ask questions, generate
code, reference files, bring in other
participants, other context, and so on. You
can do all that, but there also is another
mode in which you can use this chat.
There is this Copilot Edits
mode, as it's called.
So the name is Copilot Edits.
And what's this mode all about?
Well,
this mode here
is in the end an enhanced version of the
chat, you could say.
It is a mode that's built or that's provided
to help with multi-file editing sessions. So
as it says here, it's about editing
a set of files, multiple files
in
an easy and convenient way. It's actually a
feature inspired by
Cursor's Composer feature about which you
will learn later in the course in the Cursor
section.
The idea is that you can still ask your
questions here,
like add user authentication, if that would
be a thing you wanted to do in your
application.
And you could bring in more files that are
relevant for that query with ease by simply
using add files. And, and that's the
interesting part, when it comes to
fulfilling your request, when it comes to
answering,
this mode here will actually automatically
suggest the creation of new files and help
with multi-file code edits that are
necessary due to your prompt here.
So if I send that query, for example,
it automatically analyzes the files it
already has,
and if necessary, it would also consider
creating new files
and then suggest the specific edits that are
needed in the different files.
So this is a mode that simplifies the
process of making code changes across
multiple files. So that you don't get one
long answer where you then have to manually
copy and paste code snippets into the right
files,
but that it instead makes those edits or
suggests those edits
in multiple files automatically for you.
So this Copilot Edits mode here can be
another very interesting mode you wanna
consider using for making multi-file code
edits.
And as mentioned, it is a feature you'll
also see again later in the course, kind of
in the Cursor section, because Cursor, this
AI-powered IDE, which we'll explore in a
later section, actually pioneered this modus
or a similar feature, which will also help
with working across multiple files. But it's
good to know that it also exists here in
GitHub Copilot.
